items.title: ‘State-sanctioned theft’: Australian news outlets demand content is protected from AI scraping – as it happened
items.summary: Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastThe government will save more than it spends, says Jim Chalmers, but it won’t be a “slash and burn” budget update.Unlike the federal budget, where we get plenty of notice of when it will be handed down, the government only gives us a few days notice for the mid-financial year economic and fiscal outlook (or Myefo).There’s still a fair bit of work to do to finalise it all, but we’ve made enough progress to be confident that at this stage there will be a modest net save in the budget.We’re not going to slash and burn in the budget where that would impact the payments that people receive or where it would impact some of the more sensitive parts of the economy. But we haven’t focused the savings on just one portfolio. There will be a number of savings in the mid-year update. They will be substantial, as I said. These are serious times.You can see in the quite extraordinary reaction on the stock market just how volatile global markets are right now. items.title: Republican lawmakers break with Trump over alleged Nvidia chip smuggling after Jensen Huang’s reinstatement – as it happened
items.summary: This live blog is now closed.Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervenesSign up to the Breaking News US emailNvidia’s shares have surged by 31% at the start of trading following the news. The S+P 500 jumped 4.5% and is recovering nearly half of its brutal losses from last week, which was one of its worst since the 2008 financial crisis. Rallies for AI stocks had the Nasdaq composite up a market-leading 6.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,117 points.Here’s Trump’s full social media post, in which he also called Jensen Huang “a Great Patriot and National Treasure”.The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World! Continue reading...

items.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
items.summary: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoidedSign up for our free newsletter hereIn as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0. Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’: meet Javokhir Sindarov, the 20-year-old happy warrior moving for chess’s biggest prize
items.summary: In an exclusive interview with the Guardian ahead of the most important match of his life, the Uzbek prodigy talks Messi, GTA VI and the competitive streak he can’t switch offRead our World Chess Championship watch guideJavokhir Sindarov has a problem. The fast-rising 20-year-old Uzbek grandmaster, who is challenging for the world chess championship over the next three weeks in Switzerland, can’t stop playing for keeps. Even when he is off the clock and meant to be relaxing with friends, a compulsion to win takes hold. His preferred escape is Counter-Strike, the tactical first-person shooter that has become one of the world’s most popular esports. But he also plays EA Sports FC (née Fifa), the all-conquering soccer kickabout, and approaches both with the same seriousness of purpose that has propelled him toward the pinnacle of his day job.“I’m the guy who can’t play games just for fun,” Sindarov tells the Guardian less than 48 hours before Tuesday’s world championship opener in Geneva, smiling at the absurdity of it. “If I play something, I always try to learn, trying to become better.” Continue reading...
